:::{#hero-heading}

::: {.hero-role}
Computational Oceanographer · Assistant Professor, [University of Delaware](https://www.udel.edu/)
:::

I combine physical oceanography, data-driven methods, and high-performance computing to study fundamental multiscale ocean processes and their consequences for ecosystems and human populations.

Originally from Fortaleza (Brazil), I have a degree in Oceanography from the [Federal University of Ceará](https://www.ufc.br/) (2014), a Master's in Physical Oceanography from the [University of São Paulo](https://www5.usp.br) (2017), and a PhD in Computational Science and Engineering from the [University of Massachusetts Dartmouth](https://www.umassd.edu/) (2023).

In my free time, I love playing accordion, dancing [Forró](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forr%C3%B3), studying history, and hiking.
I am also [hemophilic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haemophilia), and I'm passionate about promoting understanding and raising awareness of rare genetic disorders.

:::

## Research

My research follows three connected lines:

::: {.research-lines}
[**1 · Data**<br>Fusion, distribution, and interpretation of large ocean datasets](research.qmd#data)

[**2 · Dynamics**<br>Multiscale physical processes in the ocean and atmosphere](research.qmd#physics)

[**3 · Impacts**<br>How multiscale physics affects ecosystems and people](research.qmd#impacts)
:::
